svg.text: One 32-bit int holds two numbers: bit 31 says "held", bits 30 to 0 count the threads waiting
In a signed int the top bit is the sign bit, so "held" and "the int is negative" are the same test: v < 0.
free, 2 still counted (just after an unlock)
Unlock adds 0x80000000. Bit 31 is 1, and 1 + 1 = 10 in binary: bit 31 becomes 0, the carry falls off the 32-bit end.
free; result is not 0, so call futex_wake
One atomic add does two jobs:
clears "held" and tells you if anyone waits.
Result 0: nobody waiting, no kernel call.
A walk through Figure 28.10 with two threads
line 4: set bit 31, old bit 0: got it (fast path, no kernel)
line 4: old bit 1: held. line 6: count + 1
line 14: v = 0x80000001 < 0. line 17: futex_wait(mutex, v): sleeps
line 8: set bit 31, old bit 0: got it. line 9: count - 1
